subtitle: How Karnataka’s village chiefs held a kingdom together

panels.shot: wide, low-angle view of a sunlit paddy landscape with tanks and a distant basadi, Gavunda of Gangavadi standing in the foreground holding a palm-leaf deed
panels.action: Gavunda of Gangavadi stands at the edge of a green field beside an earthen tank, palm-leaf grant in hand, as farmers work and a Jain basadi rises on a rocky hill behind him.

dialogue.text: In Gangavadi-96000, while kings wrote boasts on stone, the gavundas of the villages quietly kept the fields, the tanks and the temples alive.

i18n.hi: गंगवाड़ी-९६००० में, जब राजा पत्थर पर शौर्य लिखते थे, गाँवों के गौंडे चुपचाप खेत, कुंड़े और मंदिरों को जिंदा रखते थे।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view over rolling countryside with scattered hamlets, fields and a distant fort
panels.action: The countryside spreads like a patchwork of fields and hamlets, with dusty paths leading towards a modest hill-fort, as Gavunda of Gangavadi rides a small horse along a bund between tanks.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions speak of a land called Gangavadi-96000, a maze of villages and hamlets bound not just by kings, but by the men and women who held the soil.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख एक धरती का ज़िक्र करते हैं – गंगवाड़ी-९६००० – गाँवों की भूलभुलैया, जिसे राजा ही नहीं, मिट्टी संभालने वाले औरत- मर्द भी जोड़ते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot at a stone slab being inscribed, slight low angle
panels.action: Gavunda of Gangavadi stands beside a stonecutter carving Kannada script into a fresh slab, pointing to a line as a scribe reads from a palm-leaf charter under the shade of a tree.

dialogue.text: Hero stones and land grants of the Western Gangas record gavundas and pergades by name, tying their lives to taxes, ponds, temples and gifts that fixed rights in stone.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी गंगों के वीरगल्ले और दानपत्र गौंडों और पर्गडों के नाम दर्ज करते हैं, उनकी ज़िंदगी को लगान, कुंड़ों, मंदिरों और पत्थर में गड़ी हुई हकों से बाँधते हैं।

panels.shot: medium wide shot of a village assembly under a large tree
panels.action: Under a spreading tree at the edge of a village, Gavunda of Gangavadi sits on a low platform among elders and cultivators, listening as one farmer gestures anxiously towards the sky.

dialogue.text: Gavundas were village chiefs and landholders. They mediated between king and field, hearing the anxieties of cultivators and the demands of the palace.

i18n.hi: गौंडे गाँव के प्रधान और ज़मीनदार थे। वे राजा और खेत के बीच सेतु बने, हल चलाने वालों की चिन्ता और महल की माँगें दोनों सुनते थे।

panels.shot: close-up on Gavunda’s face, thoughtful, with fields blurred behind
panels.action: Gavunda of Gangavadi’s weathered face fills the frame, eyes narrowed in thought, with blurred lines of paddy and a distant tank levee behind him.

dialogue.speaker: Gavunda of Gangavadi
dialogue.text: If the rains fail, which dues can these men still bear?

i18n.hi: जब बारिश ही न हो, ये लोग और कितना कर, कितना बोझ झेलें?

dialogue.text: Inscriptions praise gavundas as loyal and generous. They are silent on the quarrels and refusals that must have tested such thoughts.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख गौंडों की वफ़ादारी और दान का गान करते हैं; झगड़ों, इंकारों और टूटने वाली दोस्ती पर वे चुप रह जाते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of irrigation tank and bund, early morning light
panels.action: Mist rises over a broad earthen tank as Gavunda of Gangavadi walks along the bund with workers, pointing to sluice gates and channels feeding terraced fields below.

dialogue.text: Across Gangavadi, tanks and canals turned summer hillsides green. Many grants name gavundas as donors or guardians of these waters.

i18n.hi: पूरी गंगवाड़ी में कुंड़े और नाले गर्मी की पहाड़ियों को हरा कर देते थे। कई दानपत्र इन पानी के दाता या राखवाल के रूप में गौंडों के नाम लिखते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a formal land grant scene in a royal hall
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, a Western Ganga king sits on a low throne while Gavunda of Gangavadi kneels respectfully, receiving a palm-leaf land grant as courtiers and scribes look on.

dialogue.text: Royal charters speak of whole villages granted as brahmadeya or temple land. A gavunda’s name often appears as witness, or as the one who would collect and remit taxes.

i18n.hi: राजादेश पूरे गाँवों को ब्रह्मदेय या देवभूमि बताते हैं। अक्सर किसी गौंडे का नाम गवाह के रूप में, या कर वसूल कर दरबार तक पहुँचाने वाले के रूप में उभरता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a countryside with multiple villages, faint lines indicating clusters, high angle
panels.action: From a hilltop, Gavunda of Gangavadi looks over several clusters of huts and fields, where faint earthen markers show boundaries between villages grouped under a single regional centre.

dialogue.text: Villages were not alone. Inscriptions mention nadus, clusters like Kogali-nadu or Belvola-nadu, where many settlements shared councils, duties and rights.

i18n.hi: गाँव अकेले नहीं थे। शिलालेख नाडु का ज़िक्र करते हैं – कोगली-नाडु, बेलवोळ-नाडु जैसे समूह, जहाँ कई बसाहटें मिलकर सभा, काम और हक बाँटती थीं।

panels.shot: medium group shot in a nadu assembly with multiple gavundas
panels.action: Several village chiefs including Gavunda of Gangavadi sit in a semi-circle inside a simple meeting hall, each holding palm-leaf documents as they debate the division of irrigation and tax burdens.

dialogue.text: At such nadu assemblies, gavundas and pergades weighed which hamlet would dig a channel, which would supply grain, which would enjoy exemption.

i18n.hi: ऐसी नाडु सभाओं में गौंडे और पर्गडे तय करते कि कौन बसाहट नाला खोडेगी, कौन अनाज देगी, किसे कर में छूट मिलेगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Jain basadi courtyard at Shravanabelagola
panels.action: In the courtyard of a Jain basadi at Shravanabelagola, monks sit in quiet conversation while Gavunda of Gangavadi and a veiled woman donor present a tray of coins and a palm-leaf deed.

dialogue.text: In Shravanabelagola’s inscriptions, gavundas appear beside Jain monks and merchant guilds, endowing basadis with land, oil and lamps in search of merit and memory.

i18n.hi: श्रवणबेलगोला के शिलालेखों में गौंडे, जैन मुनियों और व्यापारियों की संघों के साथ दिखते हैं, पुण्य और याद के लिए बसदियों को ज़मीन, तेल और दीप अर्पित करते हुए।

panels.shot: close-up of a woman’s hand and arm wearing simple bangles, placing a small donation bowl near a stone image
panels.action: A woman’s hand, bangles glinting, gently sets a small metal bowl of coins at the base of a Jain image, as Gavunda of Gangavadi watches with a respectful tilt of his head.

dialogue.text: The same stone records women as donors—wives, sisters, daughters of gavundas—gifting villages, oil, or jewels to ensure rituals and remembrance.

i18n.hi: उसी पत्थर पर औरतों के नाम भी दाता के रूप में हैं—गौंडों की पत्नियाँ, बहनें, बेटियाँ—जो गाँव, तेल या गहने देती हैं ताकि पूजा और यादें चलती रहें।

panels.shot: medium shot of engraver carving a nishidhi stone on a hill at Shravanabelagola
panels.action: On a rocky slope at Shravanabelagola, an engraver chisels a nishidhi memorial on a stone face as Gavunda of Gangavadi and a Jain monk look on, the monk’s face grave and serene.

dialogue.text: Nishidhi stones tell of sallekhana, the Jain fast unto death, celebrated in polished phrases. They do not reveal every fear, argument or pressure that may have surrounded such decisions.

i18n.hi: निशिधि शिलालेख सल्लेखना – जैन संथारा – को चकाचौंध शब्दों में सजाते हैं; वे हर डर, तकरार या दबाव को नहीं दिखाते जो ऐसे फ़ैसलों के पीछे रहा होगा।

panels.shot: medium shot of a hero stone being raised in a village clearing
panels.action: Villagers strain with ropes to raise a carved hero stone in a clearing, while Gavunda of Gangavadi directs them, and women watch from the shade, faces a mix of pride and quiet worry.

dialogue.text: Other stones praise men who died defending cattle, fields or village honour. The words are lofty; the labour of those left behind is only hinted at in the scene.

i18n.hi: दूसरे पत्थर उन मर्दों की तारीफ़ करते हैं जो गौ, खेत या गाँव की इज़्ज़त बचाते हुए मरे। बातें ऊँची हैं; पीछे छूटे लोगों की मेहनत बस दृश्य में हल्के से झलकती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a field dispute, two farmers arguing as the gavunda intervenes
panels.action: Two farmers argue at the edge of a paddy, each pointing to the same narrow strip of land, as Gavunda of Gangavadi stands between them, gesturing towards a stone boundary marker.

dialogue.text: Some inscriptions hint at disputes—encroachments on temple land, quarrels over bunds—where gavundas enforced boundaries, sometimes with fines, sometimes with persuasion.

i18n.hi: कुछ शिलालेख झगड़ों की आहट देते हैं—मंदिर की ज़मीन पर क़ब्ज़ा, बाँध पर लड़ाइयाँ—जहाँ गौंडे कभी जुर्माना, कभी समझा-बुझाकर हदें तय करवाते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of peasants working in fields with a temple and tank in background, mid-day sun
panels.action: Under the hot sun, lines of peasants transplant seedlings in a flooded field, while beyond them rise the walls of a temple and the embankment of a large tank watched over by Gavunda of Gangavadi.

dialogue.text: Karashima and Stein read these records and see an order where temple estates, tanks and local chiefs organized labour and surplus, even as peasants’ own voices remain largely unrecorded.

i18n.hi: कराशिमा और स्टाइन इन रिकॉर्डों में एक ऐसा जाल देखते हैं जहाँ देवस्थल, कुंड़े और देसी मुखिया मिलकर मेहनत और बचत को बाँधते थे, जबकि किसानों की सीधी आवाज़ ज़्यादातर गुम है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a pergade overseeing artisans and masons at work
panels.action: A pergade official gestures to masons and carpenters at a construction site, while Gavunda of Gangavadi watches, arms folded, as beams are lifted and stone blocks are aligned.

dialogue.text: Pergades appear as supervisors and strongmen, helping gavundas mobilize artisans, guards or labour gangs when a new tank, shrine or road had to be built.

i18n.hi: पर्गडे नज़र आते हैं निगरानी और ताकत के लोग बनकर, जो गौंडों की मदद से कारीगर, पहरेदार या मज़दूर टोलियाँ जुटाते, जब नया कुंड, देवालय या सड़क उठानी होती।

panels.shot: close-up of an inscription surface, letters worn but legible, with Gavunda’s shadow falling over it
panels.action: The worn face of an old stone inscription fills the frame, its Kannada letters softened by time, while the faint shadow of Gavunda of Gangavadi seems to fall across it from the side.

dialogue.text: Settar reads in Shravanabelagola’s nishidhis not only faith, but politics, family strategy and the search for prestige anchored in shared memory.

i18n.hi: सेट्टार को श्रवणबेलगोला के निशिधियों में सिर्फ़ आस्था नहीं, बल्कि राजनीति, पारिवारिक चालें और साझा याद में जड़ जमाती प्रतिष्ठा की तलाश भी पढ़ाई देती है।

panels.shot: wide sunset shot of Shravanabelagola hill with basadis and scattered stones
panels.action: As the sun sets, Shravanabelagola hill glows in orange light, its basadis silhouetted, while scattered hero stones and nishidhis dot the foreground near Gavunda of Gangavadi, who stands quietly observing.

dialogue.text: Around Shravanabelagola, fields, tanks, basadis and stones together show how a kingdom’s life ran through local hands, through gavundas and patrons whose names outlived them.

i18n.hi: श्रवणबेलगोला के आस-पास खेत, कुंड़े, बसदियाँ और पत्थर मिलकर दिखाते हैं कि राज्य की धड़कन कैसे स्थानीय हाथों से चलती थी—गौंडों और दानियों के ज़रिए जिनके नाम मौत के बाद भी जिए।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Gavunda looking over a ploughed field at dawn, contemplative
panels.action: At dawn, Gavunda of Gangavadi stands at the edge of a freshly ploughed field, hands resting on a staff, as the first light catches the furrows stretching towards a distant temple.

dialogue.text: The Western Ganga kings are remembered in chronicles, yet it is the quiet work of gavundas—holding land, law and water together—that still shapes how villages live on these hillsides today.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी गंगा राजा काव्यों में याद हैं, पर आज भी पहाड़ियों के इन गाँवों की ज़िंदगी पर वही चुपचाप चलने वाला गौंडों का काम—ज़मीन, क़ानून और पानी को साथ बाँधना—अपनी छाप छोड़ता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Karnataka’s village chiefs held a kingdom together
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे कर्नाटक के गाँव-मुखिया ने राज्य जोड़े रखा
